title: Cross-KV-slab unmap causing progressive GPU resident page growth under continuous batching
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Symptom: Certain heavy continuous-batching workloads show steady GPU resident page growth (OOMs after 12-24 hours) even though application-level allocations look constant. This reproduces most reliably on p4d nodes with cuda>=12.2 and the nvvm allocator path (cudaMallocAsync enabled). The pattern differs from previous KV-cache leaks: resident pages increase even when slab free lists appear stable. Initial hypothesis is that periodic cross-slab unmap or mempool trimming combined with KV cache eviction causes micro-fragmentation and orphaned device pages retained by the OS or driver (resident without active allocation), exacerbated by stream synchronization windows during large batch flushes.
steps_to_reproduce: Deploy a model serving job using continuous batching with max_batch_size=256 and batching_timeout=40ms on p4d instance pool
Enable KV cache with sticky prefix caching and allow aggressive eviction (kv.max_entries=100k)
Run synthetic traffic that alternates long sequences (>=2048 tokens) with short sequences (<=64 tokens) to exercise KV cache churn
Observe nvidia-smi and /proc/<pid>/smaps repeatedly over 24 hours; watch for growing Rss/Resident set and increasing CUDA driver reported reserved pages
Re-run with RMM_SILENT=1 and cudaMallocAsync=0 to confirm divergence in behavior
investigation_findings: Turning off cudaMallocAsync significantly reduces resident growth in reproduced runs; suggests allocator path is involved
Slab pool free list counters in our telemetry do not drop correspondingly when resident pages increase — implies pages are held outside of our slab accounting (driver/OS-owned arenas)
Heap snapshots using cudaMemGetInfo before/after mempool trims show transient increases in device reserved memory even when application shows free blocks
There are periodic 1-2 second stream syncs during large batch flushes that appear correlated with peaks in page residency growth
App-level KV eviction code calls cudaFree on older KV tensors during the same flush window; interleaving with allocator trim seems to leave pages in driver arenas
experiments: Experiment A: Disable cudaMallocAsync -> steady memory over 48h (no leak)
Experiment B: Patch allocator to call cudaMemPoolTrim after large free spikes -> reduced long-term growth but increased short-term fragmentation and latency spikes
Experiment C: Introduce staggered KV eviction (randomized delays) -> smoothed resident growth but not eliminated
Experiment D: Force explicit cudaMemPoolSetAttribute (trim aggressiveness) on every Nth eviction -> mitigates accumulation on some nodes, fails on older driver versions
Experiment E: Add per-stream serialization around KV free calls -> decreased correlation between sync windows and resident growth
proposed_fix: Short-term (hotfix): Add guarded call to cudaMemPoolTrim after large KV eviction batches, gated behind rollout flag; monitor latency/regression
Medium-term: Implement allocator-aware KV free path that coalesces freed pages and annotates them to the driver mempool to avoid leaving orphaned pages
Long-term: Add allocator telemetry hooks exposing per-mempool reserved/resident deltas and driver arena attribution; add automated trimming policy tuned by workload patterns
Fallback: On nodes with older drivers where trim is ineffective, automatically disable cudaMallocAsync for serving pool and switch to pooled cudaMalloc path
blockers: Driver behavior variance across CUDA 11.x / 12.x — need QA matrix and infra for repro on multiple driver versions
Potential latency regressions caused by aggressive mempool trims — need perf signoff from SRE
Some clusters are managed by partners (on-prem) and cannot be quickly instrumented; limited access for low-level driver logs
